Most futures traders stare at spot prices. The professional commodity desks ignore them. 📊

Here's what dominates commodity futures returns... and it isn't price direction.

It's the shape of the curve.

Erb & Harvey (RFS, 2006) and Koijen, Moskowitz, Pedersen & Vrugt (JFE, 2018) documented carry as a single, unified factor priced across asset classes. In commodities, it works like this:

🔹 RANK every commodity by annualized roll yield (the slope between front and second contract).
🔹 LONG the most BACKWARDATED. These pay you to hold them.
🔹 SHORT the most CONTANGOED. These bleed you on every roll.
🔹 DOLLAR-NEUTRAL, monthly rebalance, ~20-30 commodities across energy, metals, grains, softs, livestock.

Why it persists: storage costs, hedging pressure from producers, and convenience yield create a structural slope. That slope is the reward, not the price move.

Peer-reviewed across 4 decades. Replicated globally. Still works because the underlying flows (hedgers needing to lock in prices) don't go away.
